recommendation: Keep this commit as the completion of the applied FHIR-18122 change. If Financial Management wants a different element name or target-resource set than the historical authorizer/source request, handle that as a new forward-looking Jira decision.
issue_request: FHIR-18122 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Coverage change request, raised and applied for STU3. It requested Coverage.costToBeneficiary.exception 0..* with a required type CodeableConcept, an optional validity period, and an optional reference to the authorizer/source of the exception.
initial_application: Commit 7fbe7046270ff6857644a6af63207642576dc7ef explicitly included #18122 and added the exception backbone, type and period children, example financial-exception terminology, and an example instance. Later source migration commits preserved those pieces, but no source or history evidence showed the requested authorized/source child ever being added.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-27024, already represented on the combined branch, relies on Coverage.costToBeneficiary.exception and confirms that the exception backbone remains current. Targeted Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later decision reversing the authorizer/source requirement. The Jira resolution named ProviderRole, which is not an active current-build resource; PractitionerRole is the current role resource alongside Organization.
reconciliation: Added Coverage.costToBeneficiary.exception.authorized as an optional Reference(PractitionerRole|Organization) in source/coverage/structuredefinition-Coverage.xml.
